title: Squassux Landing / Squassucks Point
summary: Squassux Landing / Squassucks Point is a Carmans River mouth placename tied to Unkechaug history, clay beds, pottery, ferry landings, and local memory at Brookhaven.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Unkechaug Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Named for an Indigenous potter who lived and worked near the mouth of Carman's River, Squassux Landing originally served as a strategic launch point for Native Americans hunting whales along the barrier beach. Recognizing the evolution of this site into a busy staging area for later commercial whaling crews illustrates how longstanding Indigenous maritime skills laid the foundation for Long Island's most famous historic industry.
introduction_content: Squassucks is recorded as a point of land in Brookhaven on the East Connecticut River, now generally associated with the Carmans River mouth.
history_content: The name is connected with Wisquosuck, an Unkechaug pot maker who lived on the point. Later local use remembers the place as Squassux Landing near the river mouth and bay crossing.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Squassucks, Squassux, Wisquosuck, Wesquasesac, Wisguassuck, and Wisquoriake. The personal name is interpreted as pot maker.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names are often rooted in experiences and sensory impressions. They describe the characteristics of the landscape, available resources, and historical events.”

— Ekaterina Mikhailova, The Importance of Indigenous Place Names (2025), A Living Tradition section
preservation_content: Squassux Landing preserves a personal name and a river-mouth place-name tied to Unkechaug presence, pottery, land records, and south-shore travel.
land_loss_content: Squassux Landing and all the land that includes today's South Haven, Brookhaven, and Bellport were purchased from the Unkechaugs in 1664. [1. A Brief History of Squassux Landing, Fire Place Brookhaven Village Association Spring 2013 Newsletter, pp. 1]
